action_apply_manifest: Applies a raw Kubernetes manifest (YAML/JSON) to the cluster after a safety review.
action_execute_command: Runs a shell command inside a pod's container — essentially `kubectl exec`.
action_restart_workload: Rolling-restarts a deployment / statefulset / daemonset without changing its spec.
action_rollback_deployment: Reverts a deployment to a previous revision after a bad rollout.
analyze_blast_radius: Given a resource, shows everything that would be impacted if it crashed — dependents, traffic, data loss risk.
analyze_capacity_trends: Looks at CPU / memory / pod-count over time to predict when the cluster needs more capacity.
analyze_cronjob_health: Scans CronJobs for missed schedules, failed runs, and suspended jobs.
analyze_daemonset_health: Checks that each DaemonSet has a pod on every eligible node and all are Ready.
analyze_dependencies: Maps which services depend on which, so you can see the blast-radius of a change.
analyze_deployment_health: Checks if deployments have the right number of ready replicas and flags ones that are degraded.
analyze_error_correlation: Correlates errors across events, logs, and metrics to find the root cause.
analyze_failure_patterns: Looks for recurring failure patterns — the same thing going wrong over and over.
analyze_hpa_behavior: Looks at HPA scale events over time to see if scaling is jumpy, stuck, or well-tuned.
analyze_image_vulnerabilities: Scans the container images running in the cluster for known CVEs.
analyze_ingress_health: Checks every ingress: backend exists, endpoints ready, TLS certs valid, recent 5xx rate.
analyze_job_health: Scans Jobs for stuck ones, failing retry loops, and jobs that never complete.
analyze_log_patterns: Groups recent log lines into clusters so frequent error signatures pop out.
analyze_network_connectivity: Checks DNS, services, and NetworkPolicies for connectivity gaps.
analyze_node_pressure: Looks for nodes under CPU / memory / disk pressure that might start evicting pods.
analyze_performance_bottlenecks: Finds the slowest pods, the hottest nodes, and the chokepoints in between.
analyze_pod_health: Checks every pod for common problems — restarts, OOM kills, image-pull errors, CrashLoopBackOff — and summarizes in plain language.
analyze_pod_scheduling: Explains why pods are landing where they are — node selectors, affinity, taints, spread.
analyze_rbac_permissions: Reviews who has access to what in the cluster and flags overly-broad bindings.
analyze_replicaset_health: Checks ReplicaSets for the gap between desired and ready replicas and why.
analyze_resource_efficiency: Compares requested resources against actual usage to find overprovisioned workloads.
analyze_rollout_risk: Assesses how risky the next rollout of a deployment is based on recent history + blast radius.
analyze_service_health: Checks every service: has endpoints, selector works, traffic is flowing.
analyze_statefulset_health: Inspects StatefulSets for ordering issues, stuck replicas, and PVC mount failures.
analyze_storage_health: Checks persistent-volume claims — are they bound, are they full, are any in an error state.
analyze_workload_patterns: Clusters workloads by their usage profile — batch vs steady vs spiky.
apply_resource_patch: Applies a strategic-merge or JSON patch to a single resource.
assess_security_posture: High-level check of the cluster's security hygiene — pod security, RBAC, secrets, network.
automation_create_alert_rule: Generates a Prometheus-style alert rule for a condition you describe.
automation_generate_runbook: Generates a plain-English runbook for an incident type, based on cluster state.
automation_run_playbook: Executes a named runbook end-to-end, stopping for approval on destructive steps.
automation_schedule_task: Schedules a recurring task (a CronJob / alert / report).
check_capabilities_all_added: Flags containers that add the ALL or SYS_ADMIN Linux capability — essentially root with a different name.
check_default_service_accounts_in_use: Workloads using the 'default' ServiceAccount when they should have a dedicated, least-privilege one.
check_host_path_mounts: Lists pods mounting host paths, the classic container-to-host escape surface.
check_image_tag_latest: Workloads whose images have no tag or are pinned to :latest — unreproducible rollouts waiting to happen.
check_ingress_tls_expiry_30d: TLS certificates behind your ingresses that will expire within 30 days. Uses the backend's /tls-info endpoint.
check_privileged_containers: Flags pods running privileged containers or using hostNetwork/hostPID — the hardest escape-risks in Kubernetes.
check_rbac_wildcards: Role and ClusterRole rules with '*' verbs or resources — a standing invitation to privilege escalation.
check_resource_limits: Flags containers with no CPU / memory limits set (an operational foot-gun).
check_root_containers: Finds containers that may run as UID 0 because runAsNonRoot isn't set true.
check_secrets_in_env: Containers that read Secret values via env variables — prefer file mounts so logs can't leak them.
check_writable_root_fs: Finds containers without a read-only root filesystem — a defense-in-depth control you almost always want.
cordon_node: Marks a node unschedulable so new pods don't land there.
cost_analyze_spending: Breaks down where cluster spend is going right now — by namespace, workload, node.
cost_forecast_spending: Projects cluster cost N days out based on current growth trend.
cost_identify_waste: Finds the dollar-value waste — idle workloads, released volumes, over-provisioned requests.
cost_optimization_plan: Composes a ranked list of cost-reduction actions with estimated $ saved per action.
delete_resource: Deletes a specific resource by kind + name. Safety-gated.
detect_configuration_drift: Finds resources whose live spec has drifted from what's in source control / last known good.
detect_resource_contention: Pairs of pods fighting over the same node's CPU / memory / IO / network.
diagnose_certificate_failures: Lists cert-manager Certificate and CertificateRequest failure events in the window, with reasons.
diagnose_cronjob_missing_runs: Explains why a CronJob didn't fire recently — suspended, concurrency conflict, or never scheduled.
diagnose_deployment_rollback_needed: Compares current revision to the prior one and tells you if the new rollout is worse than what it replaced.
diagnose_hpa_not_scaling: Why isn't the autoscaler scaling? Checks min=max, missing metrics, and unreachable targets in conditions.
diagnose_ingress_404: Traces an ingress path to backend service to endpoints and reports which link in the chain is broken.
diagnose_networkpolicy_blocking: Detects default-deny network policies and flags when a manual trace is needed to decide if a specific flow is blocked.
diagnose_node_unschedulable: Tells you why pods won't land on a node — cordoned, tainted, or under memory/disk/PID pressure.
diagnose_pod_not_ready: Tells you exactly why a specific pod isn't Ready — CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff, probe failures, or still Pending.
diagnose_pvc_pending: Walks through why a PVC is stuck Pending — missing storage class, no matching volume, or provisioner failing.
diagnose_service_no_endpoints: Explains why a service has no backends — selector mismatch, no pods running, or the service is headless.
drain_node: Evicts all pods off a node in prep for maintenance, honoring PodDisruptionBudgets.
export_topology_to_drawio: Exports the cluster topology as a draw.io / diagrams.net file for slides or docs.
get_cluster_health: Gives a plain-English summary of whether the cluster looks healthy right now: node count, pod statuses, obvious problems.
get_events: Lists recent Kubernetes events — useful for 'why did my pod fail?' or 'what happened in the last hour?'
get_logs: Gets recent log lines from a pod, so you can see what the application actually said or errored out with.
get_resource: Gets the full details of one specific thing (a single pod, a single deployment) when you need to see everything about it.
inspect_clusterrole: Everything about a ClusterRole: rules, who's bound to it, blast radius.
inspect_clusterrolebinding: A ClusterRoleBinding's subjects, the role they grant, and what it lets them do.
inspect_configmap: A ConfigMap's data, which pods mount it, and recent changes.
inspect_crd: A CRD's schema, scope, versions, and the custom resources it owns.
inspect_cronjob: A CronJob's schedule, last run status, active jobs, recent events, ownership chain.
inspect_daemonset: A DaemonSet's spec, which nodes run it, pod status per node, recent events.
inspect_deployment: One-call deep dive into a Deployment: spec, rollout status, events, owned ReplicaSets.
inspect_hpa: An HPA's target, metrics, current vs desired replicas, recent scale events.
inspect_ingress: An Ingress's rules, TLS config, backend services, recent events.
inspect_job: A Job's spec, completions, active pods, failed retries, events.
inspect_limitrange: A LimitRange's enforced min/max values per container / pod / pvc.
inspect_namespace: A namespace's pod / workload inventory, quotas, events, current usage.
inspect_networkpolicy: A NetworkPolicy's selectors, ingress/egress rules, and the pods it applies to.
inspect_node: One-call deep dive into a Node: capacity, conditions, taints, pods, events.
inspect_pdb: A PodDisruptionBudget's selector, minAvailable / maxUnavailable, and the workloads it covers.
inspect_pod: One-call deep dive into a Pod: spec, status, containers, events, ownership chain.
inspect_pv: A PV's capacity, reclaim policy, current PVC binding, storage class.
inspect_pvc: A PVC's phase, storage class, bound PV, and consuming pods.
inspect_replicaset: A ReplicaSet's desired/ready/available replicas, its parent Deployment, and its pods.
inspect_resourcequota: A ResourceQuota's hard limits and current usage per resource type.
inspect_role: A Role's rules, who's bound to it, and what operations it enables.
inspect_rolebinding: A RoleBinding's subjects, the role it grants, and effective permissions.
inspect_secret: A Secret's metadata, which pods mount it, type, and recent changes. Never returns raw values.
inspect_service: A Service's selector, ports, endpoints, traffic policy, and recent events.
inspect_statefulset: A StatefulSet's spec, ordinal pod status, PVC templates, update strategy, events.
inspect_storageclass: A StorageClass's provisioner, parameters, reclaim policy, and bound PVs.
inspect_vpa: A VerticalPodAutoscaler's recommendations vs current requests, and update mode.
list_resources: Shows you a list of things in your cluster — pods, services, anything. Tell it 'list pods' and it fetches them straight from Kubernetes.
narrate_capacity_report: Cluster-wide capacity: per-node utilization, headroom, whether a hypothetical new workload fits, trend direction.
narrate_change_impact: What-if analysis: given a proposed change, reasons through first- and second-order effects on the cluster.
narrate_cost_report: Cost breakdown by namespace or workload, with the single biggest driver and biggest cut opportunity.
narrate_deploy_diff: Explains in plain words what changed between a deployment's last two revisions and what users are likely seeing.
narrate_incident_timeline: Turns the last hour of events into a Slack-ready chronological story of what broke and when.
narrate_migration_readiness: What you'd have to move to migrate a namespace: workloads, PVCs, config, secrets, and known risks.
narrate_onboarding_for_user: What a specific ServiceAccount can actually touch — roles, resources, verbs, namespaces. Flags cluster-admin.
narrate_security_posture: CISO-ready posture summary — pod security, network policies, RBAC, secrets — with one next step each.
narrate_service_dependency_graph: Describes what calls a service and what it calls in turn, including the policies gating each hop.
narrate_weekly_status: An exec-friendly weekly cluster status — health headline, top changes, top issues, a few call-outs.
observe_api_resources: Lists every API resource type the cluster knows about — including CRDs.
observe_cluster_overview: A dashboard-style snapshot of the whole cluster: what's running, what's broken, at-a-glance numbers.
observe_configmap_consumers: Which pods mount or reference a given ConfigMap.
observe_custom_resources: Lists all custom-resource instances of a given CRD.
observe_deployment_detailed: Everything about one deployment: replicas, pods, rollout status, recent changes.
observe_deployment_rollout_history: The revision history of a deployment with cause + timestamp per revision.
observe_events: Recent Kubernetes events — OOM kills, scheduling failures, rolled out, unhealthy, and more.
observe_flapping_services: Finds services whose endpoints keep churning — a sign pods behind them are unstable or being rescheduled.
observe_high_cardinality_labels: Would flag label keys with more than a thousand distinct values (Prometheus risk); backend index not yet available.
observe_ingresses_by_tls_expiry: Ingresses sorted by how close their TLS cert is to expiring.
observe_metrics: Raw pod + node metrics from metrics-server — CPU millicores and memory.
observe_missing_probes: Flags workloads whose containers have neither liveness nor readiness probes — you're flying blind there.
observe_namespace_detailed: Deep dive into a namespace — every pod, every service, every config, plus recent changes.
observe_namespace_overview: Zoom in on one namespace: what's running inside it, resource usage, recent events.
observe_network_policies: All NetworkPolicies in scope with their selector and ingress/egress rule summary.
observe_node_detailed: Everything about a single node: its pods, capacity, conditions, what's failing if anything.
observe_node_metrics: CPU / memory usage for every node right now.
observe_node_status: Is this node healthy? Are disks / memory / CPU under pressure?
observe_noisy_neighbors: Shows pods eating more than 80% of a node's CPU or memory — the ones starving their neighbors.
observe_orphaned_pods: Finds pods whose owning ReplicaSet or Job is gone — leftovers from a partial delete or controller bug.
observe_pending_scheduler_events: Shows recent FailedScheduling events so you can see which pods can't land and why — taint, affinity, or capacity.
observe_pod_dependencies: Everything a pod depends on — ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, Services — and what depends on it.
observe_pod_detailed: Deep dive into a single pod: containers, status, restarts, resource usage, recent events.
observe_pod_events: Just the events that mention a specific pod — scheduled, started, killed, restarted, etc.
observe_pod_logs: Fetches logs for a specific pod with filtering by tail size or time window.
observe_pod_logs_filtered: Pod logs filtered to only error- or warn-level lines.
observe_pod_metrics: CPU / memory usage for one pod or across the cluster.
observe_pvc_consumers: Which pods currently use a given PVC.
observe_recent_changes: Every meaningful cluster change in a time window — rollouts, scales, config updates, failures.
observe_resource: Full details of a specific Kubernetes resource by kind + namespace + name.
observe_resource_history: Previous versions of a resource (if tracked), with diff between revisions.
observe_resource_links: What a resource links to and what links to it — the dependency edges.
observe_resource_topology: Graph view of related resources around a starting resource.
observe_resources_by_query: Finds resources matching a natural-language query, like 'failing pods in production'.
observe_restart_storms: Lists containers whose cumulative restart count is above threshold — the ones CrashLoopBackOff-ing hardest.
observe_secret_consumers: Which pods mount or reference a given Secret.
observe_secrets_usage: Cluster-wide view of which Secrets are actually used, stale, or referenced-but-missing.
observe_service_endpoints: The backing endpoints (IPs + ports) for a Service right now.
observe_serviceaccount_detailed: A ServiceAccount's secrets, bound roles, and the pods using it.
observe_serviceaccount_permissions: Exactly what a ServiceAccount can do across the cluster.
observe_services_by_filter: Services filtered by selector label, port, type, or recent issues.
observe_storage_status: Cluster-wide storage health — PVs, PVCs, classes, capacity, errors.
observe_stuck_rollouts: Surfaces deployments that have been 'progressing' for more than ten minutes without any new replicas becoming ready.
observe_top_pods_by_metric: Top N pods sorted by a metric (CPU, memory, network, or events).
observe_unhealthy_probes: Lists pods whose liveness or readiness probes are failing right now, grouped so the noise is denoised.
observe_workload_health: A high-level 'is my workload healthy?' check across deployments, statefulsets, daemonsets.
observe_zombie_finalizers: Finds resources stuck in Terminating longer than ten minutes because a finalizer won't release them.
plan_backup_coverage: Lists workloads that store data in PVCs but have no backup label or schedule — backup gaps you probably didn't know about.
plan_cost_reduction: Looks for idle nodes, orphaned persistent volumes, and over-replicated workloads so you can cut spend without pain.
plan_drain_node: Before you drain a node, see which pods would evict, which PDBs you'd break, and whether other nodes can absorb the work.
plan_ha_upgrade: Finds single-replica workloads that would die if a node blinks, and tells you how to make them highly-available.
plan_image_pull_secrets: Finds the same pull secret cloned across many namespaces and recommends a consolidated pattern.
plan_pdb_coverage: Deployments and StatefulSets with multiple replicas that lack a PodDisruptionBudget, with a suggested minAvailable for each.
plan_psa_enforcement: Which namespaces can safely tighten to restricted pod security? Names the pods that would need to change first.
plan_resource_quota: Suggests ResourceQuota limits per namespace based on what each one actually uses today, padded for growth.
plan_rollout_safety: Estimates how risky rolling out a new image tag is — who consumes this service, are replicas ready, what's the safe canary percentage.
plan_scale_deployment: Given observed load, tells you what replica count would put utilization in the healthy band — and flags when HPA is maxed out.
recommend_architecture_improvements: Suggests architectural improvements based on what's running and how it behaves.
recommend_cost_reduction: Ranked list of changes that would cut cost with minimal risk.
recommend_disaster_recovery: Assesses DR posture and recommends backup schedules, cross-AZ spread, and failover drills.
recommend_monitoring_improvements: Gaps in observability — missing alerts, unmonitored probes, missing dashboards.
recommend_resource_optimization: Rightsizing suggestions: which containers should request more / less CPU or memory.
recommend_scaling_strategy: Recommends HPA / VPA / KEDA configuration for each workload based on its load profile.
recommend_security_hardening: Specific security controls to turn on, prioritized by risk reduction.
recommend_upgrade_path: Suggests a safe Kubernetes version upgrade path given current cluster state.
resolve_resource: Given a kind and a fuzzy name, finds the actual namespace + full name.
restart_pod: Deletes a pod so its controller spins up a fresh replacement.
rollback_deployment: Rolls a deployment back to its previous revision.
security_audit_rbac: End-to-end RBAC audit — cluster-admin bindings, wildcard rules, stale accounts.
security_check_pod_security: Scans every pod against pod-security-standards (privileged / baseline / restricted).
security_compliance_report: Maps findings to compliance frameworks: CIS, SOC2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS.
security_scan_cluster: Comprehensive cluster-level security scan covering CIS benchmark controls.
security_scan_secrets: Looks for secret hygiene issues: plaintext, over-mounted, old, unused.
trigger_hpa_scale: Nudges an HPA to re-evaluate metrics and scale now instead of waiting.
troubleshoot_deployment_failures: Autonomous investigation of a failing deployment — pod events, rollout history, logs.
troubleshoot_network_issues: Traces a connectivity problem across DNS, services, endpoints, and NetworkPolicies.
troubleshoot_performance_degradation: Correlates slow-down symptoms with metrics, events, and recent changes.
troubleshoot_pod_failures: End-to-end investigation of why a pod keeps failing, with suggested fixes.
troubleshoot_rbac_issues: Traces 'Forbidden' errors back to the missing RBAC rule and who could grant it.
troubleshoot_resource_constraints: Correlates OOM / throttle / pressure events with resource requests + limits.
troubleshoot_storage_issues: Walks PV / PVC / mount / provisioner errors to pinpoint storage failures.
update_resource_limits: Updates a container's CPU / memory requests + limits without a full rollout.
who_can_do: Given a verb + resource, lists which service accounts / users can do it.
